title: How rich is Africa?
subtitle: There is no single answer: income per person in 2023 ran from $250 in Burundi to $18,131 in Seychelles.

parts.text: Africa is often described as one economy, poor and uniform. The numbers cannot be summed up in one phrase.
In 2023 gross domestic product per person, in current US dollars, was about $250 in Burundi and about $18,131 in Seychelles.
The highest is about 73 times the lowest, a ratio calculated here.
The middle country of the 52 with a figure was at about $1,709.
Eight countries were above $5,000 and sixteen below $1,000, counted here.
Eritrea and South Sudan have no figure for 2023.
GDP per person divides a country's total output by its population. It does not say how income is shared, what things cost, or how much work happens outside the market.
It is a starting point for asking questions, not a verdict on any place.

gaps: GDP per capita in current US dollars depends on exchange rates, so it can move without anyone's life changing. Other measures, such as purchasing-power comparisons, give a different spread and are not used here.
The summary figures are our own arithmetic on one year's World Bank values; a different year would change them.
Nothing here covers inequality inside countries, which can be as wide as the gap between them.
